items.purpose: Pursuant to the provisions of H. Res. 405, the respective amendments in the nature of a substitute recommended by the Committee on the Judiciary now printed in each bill is considered adopted.

dimensions.assessment: Affects qualified active and retired law enforcement officers nationwide, as well as state, local, and federal entities managing public properties and facilities.
dimensions.evidence: allows qualified active and retired law enforcement officers to carry concealed firearms and ammunition

dimensions.assessment: Changes the legal ability of specified officers to carry weapons in restricted areas such as school zones and certain federal facilities, and allows states to modify retirement qualification timelines.
dimensions.evidence: permits states to reduce the frequency with which retired law enforcement officers must meet certain qualification standards.

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not mention specific federal spending, revenue changes, or detailed economic impacts.
Amends Title 18 of the United States Code concerning firearms, school zones, national parks, and federal facility security levels.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 18, United States Code, to improve the Law Enforcement Officer Safety Act

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory amendments to federal law affecting law enforcement carrying rights nationwide.

missing_information: Specific estimates of federal fiscal or budgetary costs
Exact number of active and retired law enforcement officers affected
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends federal law to broaden the authority of qualified active and retired law enforcement officers to carry concealed firearms and ammunition across various public and federal spaces, and allows states to extend the interval for retired officers' firearm qualification standards up to 36 months.

related.label: H.Res. 405
related.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2240) to require the Attorney General to develop reports relating to violent attacks against law enforcement officers, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2243) to amend title 18, United States Code, to improve the Law Enforcement Officer Safety Act and provisions relating to the carrying of concealed weapons by law enforcement officers, and for other purposes; and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2255) to allow Federal law enforcement officers to purchase retired service weapons, and for other purposes.
